about_blocks.text: Canadian Therapy is a private psychotherapy practice based in Toronto. It is not a residential rehab. There are no beds, no detox and no live-in program. Clients book 50-minute sessions with a Registered Psychotherapist or Registered Social Worker, and most of those sessions happen online by secure video, which means anyone in Ontario can use the service.

about_blocks.text: The practice was founded by Preeti Taneja, a Registered Social Worker who still sees clients as lead therapist. She set it up for people who want a therapist who understands their culture, and South Asian, immigrant and BIPOC clients make up a large part of the people it serves. Between them, the therapists speak English, Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Farsi and French.

about_blocks.text: Substance use is one area of the work rather than the whole of it. The practice lists addiction, alcohol abuse and codependency among its services, and several therapists on the team name addiction as a focus, using approaches such as cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT), acceptance and commitment therapy and internal family systems. The same team also works with anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, burnout, ADHD and family conflict, which helps when drinking or drug use is tangled up with something else.

about_blocks.text: Couples and family sessions are available too. A couples session runs 55 minutes, and an extended relationship session of 90 minutes lets two or more people meet together. For people whose drinking or drug use is straining a marriage or a parent relationship, that can be a practical place to start.

about_blocks.text: In-person appointments are possible in Toronto with three of the therapists for an extra $30 a session. The practice's business address is 477 Richmond Street West, and its in-person bookings list an office at 692 Euclid Avenue. Fees run from $165 to $280 per session including HST. Canadian Therapy does not bill insurers directly, but it gives you a receipt after each session to send to your extended health plan.

about_blocks.text: If you need medical detox, medication or a residential program, this is not the right first stop on its own. The therapists cannot prescribe, though the practice says it can refer you to a mental health physician. For ongoing counselling alongside other care, or for help before and after a stay elsewhere, it is a reasonable option.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Canadian Therapy

faqs.question: Is Canadian Therapy a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. Canadian Therapy is an outpatient psychotherapy practice, and most sessions take place online. It has no beds, detox or overnight program. You book individual, couples or family sessions and continue your normal life between them.
answer_blocks.html: No. Canadian Therapy is an outpatient psychotherapy practice, and most sessions take place online. It has no beds, detox or overnight program. You book individual, couples or family sessions and continue your normal life between them.

faqs.question: Does Canadian Therapy help with addiction and alcohol use?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. The practice lists addiction, alcohol abuse and codependency among its services, and therapists Shannon Kane, Miranda Elise Klimowski and Avista Amuyan name addiction as a focus. Care is talk therapy, using methods such as CBT, DBT and acceptance and commitment therapy. Medical detox and medication are not offered.

faqs.question: How much does a session cost?

answer_blocks.text: Individual sessions of 50 minutes cost between $165 and $280 including HST, depending on the therapist, and the first intake assessment starts at $185. Couples sessions start at $225 for 55 minutes, and a 90-minute extended relationship session is $325. In-person sessions add $30. The 20-minute first consultation is free.

faqs.question: Can I use my insurance or workplace benefits?

answer_blocks.text: Usually, yes. Many extended health plans in Ontario cover sessions with Registered Psychotherapists and Registered Social Workers, and the practice gives you a receipt after each session to submit yourself. It does not bill insurers directly, so check your plan's coverage before you start.

faqs.question: Is there culturally specific support for South Asian clients?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, this is a main focus of the practice. Many of its therapists are South Asian, and they offer sessions in Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam as well as English. They work with family expectations, immigration stress and shame around asking for help, which can all affect substance use.
